passages.text: Over 2 million diapering essentials donated Supporting families is our reason for being, starting with our own team and extended to our community.

Parents, this one’s for you Before launching any product or service, we ask ourselves, ”Will this make parents’ lives easier?” Your thoughts, opinions, and feedback, help us answer this—so we’re always standing by at hello@coterie.com Two dads are playing with their child who is laying on a yellow blanket.Two dads are playing with their child who is laying on a yellow blanket.Two dads are playing with their child who is laying on a yellow blanket.Two dads are playing with their child who is laying on a yellow blanket.

The brand was spending broadly on unqualified audiences while missing shoppers actively seeking solutions for specific needs—sensitive skin, overnight protection, and newborn care—that represented Coterie’s greatest growth opportunity. Coterie partnered with Envision Horizons, an Amazon Ads advanced partner that helps brands build awareness and gain market share through Amazon's advertising capabilities, to rebuild the entire audience strategy. The objective was clear: reach parents actively seeking a premium alternative who, once acquired, would become repeat buyers rather than one-time purchasers.

passages.text: Frank Yu’s Vision: Finding Opportunity in a Mature Market Coterie and Frank Yu Before launching Coterie, Frank Yu studied how successful consumer brands built loyalty. He understood that great companies do not only sell products. They sell trust, identity, and a feeling that connects with customers. When Yu examined the diaper market, he saw a category that was massive but surprisingly predictable. The biggest brands had strong distribution, decades of history, and loyal customers. However, much of the marketing looked nearly identical. Packages were filled with bright colors and playful characters, while messaging focused mainly on babies.
passages.identity_reason: third-party passage names the company in a confirmed document

passages.text: Goals Coterie, a premium baby care brand, had established strong brand awareness on Amazon but faced a fundamental audience challenge. Despite meaningful investment in advertising, the brand’s account structure was not built to reach the high-intent parent segments most likely to convert and become loyal customers. An account audit revealed the scope of the opportunity. Approximately 39% of ad spend was not generating sales, 37% of the budget was flowing into broad automatic campaigns, and 59% of campaigns were focused on a competitor strategy that was not converting.
passages.identity_reason: third-party passage names the company in a confirmed document

passages.text: Envision Horizons layered in Amazon DSP to extend the audience strategy beyond search with three tactics: view remarketing to reconnect with shoppers who had engaged but not converted, lapsed purchase remarketing to re-engage previous buyers, and cross-sell campaigns to introduce existing diaper customers to Coterie’s skincare line. At just 5.2% of total budget, Amazon DSP delivered outsized impact by maintaining connections with high-value audiences across their full purchase journey. A simultaneous Brand Store rebuild ensured that when new audiences arrived, they encountered a premium experience reinforcing Coterie’s value proposition.
passages.identity_reason: third-party passage names the company in a confirmed document

passages.text: Launching Coterie: Reinventing the Diaper Category Coterie The Future of Premium Baby Products When Coterie launched in 2019, it entered a market dominated by some of the largest consumer companies in the world. Instead of competing by copying traditional diaper brands, the company did the opposite. It removed the noise. Coterie introduced minimalist packaging, clean typography, and a modern visual identity. The brand looked less like a traditional baby product and more like a premium skincare or wellness company. This was not simply a design choice. It was a strategic decision. Coterie understood that consumers do not only purchase products based on function.
passages.identity_reason: third-party passage names the company in a confirmed document

passages.text: Introduction: The Diaper Brand That Changed an Entire Industry The Coterie success story is not about creating a completely new product. It is about seeing an old product in a completely new way. For decades, the diaper industry followed the same formula. Bright colors. Cartoon characters. Loud packaging. Marketing campaigns designed around babies. But there was one major problem: babies were never the ones making the purchase decisions. Parents were. Every year, millions of parents spend thousands of dollars buying diapers, yet many brands continue speaking to them as if they were shopping for children rather than making an important decision for their families.
